comment: Reviewed fork recipes and generic backend-family rules, embedded in ggrun and validated at load (see catalog.go). Recipe order is significant: lookups and listings follow it. Optional per-recipe fields kind, tensor_count, superseded_by, evidence and expires are defined but unused so far; required_tensor_types is read by ResolveRequirement (no shipped entry uses it yet). Patch files live under patches/ and are pinned by sha256.

recipes.name: nanbeige42
recipes.note: NanoBeige support is upstream llama.cpp, not a permanent fork. Pin the first reviewed merge commit so `ggrun support install --with-backend` can build a known architecture-capable helper backend even when the machine's normal production backend intentionally stays older. The reviewed Nanbeige4.2 GGUF predates upstream's final metadata spelling: it uses loop_count plus a logical block count, while upstream b77d646 expects num_loops plus a physical block count. The patch makes the loader support both unambiguously.
recipes.description: Upstream llama.cpp with native Nanbeige4.2 looped-transformer support

recipes.name: hy3
recipes.description: Tencent Hy3 / hy_v3 support with built-in MTP and its reviewed chat template

recipes.description: Preliminary MiniMax-M3 support with native structured tool-call parsing

recipes.name: laguna
recipes.note: Poolside's own fork, not the upstream pull request. The upstream PR (joerowell/llama.cpp @ add-laguna) serves Laguna correctly but implements only the target architecture. Its loader builds 69 of the 76 tensors the published DFlash drafter contains, so any speculative launch dies during model load: done_getting_tensors: wrong number of tensors; expected 76, got 69. Poolside state it directly: "Upstream llama.cpp ships the generic DFlash framework but not the Laguna decoder contract this draft model needs." Speculation is the largest measured lever on a RAM-resident MoE -- a forward pass costs nearly the same carrying one token or a micro-batch -- so a recipe that cannot load the drafter forfeits it. The patch: common/speculative.cpp calls std::isfinite without including <cmath>; the declaration reaches poolside's compiler transitively and ours not at all, so the fork builds for them and fails here at 95% with "'isfinite' is not a member of 'std'". Adding the include is the whole fix and changes no behaviour.
recipes.description: Poolside Laguna support including the DFlash drafter (poolside fork, not the upstream PR)

recipes.name: laguna-upstream-pr
recipes.note: Kept selectable: it is the branch heading for upstream, so it is the one to test against when the PR merges, and it remains a working target-only fallback if the poolside fork regresses.
recipes.description: Laguna target architecture from the open upstream llama.cpp PR (no DFlash drafter)

name_rules.note: minimax-m2, minimax-m3, ... require the ik_llama family. Shared by CLI preflight and the TUI so an auto continue-once choice cannot select a backend the CLI will immediately reject.
